patch_description: The current GPU-level assignment relies purely on the greedy LPT-style `balanced_packing`, which gives no post-hoc refinement (balancedness_score_gpu is only 0.66). The makespan of a bin-packing solution can typically be improved substantially with a cheap local search: after the greedy assignment, repeatedly identify the most-loaded and least-loaded GPU within each (layer, node) and swap the pair of experts between them that most reduces the load gap while preserving the fixed per-GPU slot count (each GPU must keep exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` experts, so swaps are the valid move). The search is bounded (a few iterations per row, each O(num_packs * slots²)) and operates on Python lists, so it adds negligible runtime compared to the greedy pass while directly minimizing the max-GPU-load objective that the balancedness score measures. The refined `pack_index`/`rank_in_pack` are then fed into the existing `phy2pphy` computation, so downstream logic is unchanged.
